text: Vikram S. Buddhi, born on May 10, 1971, is an Indian Ph.D. student and teaching assistant at Purdue University who was convicted in 2007 for making death threats online against U.S. President George W. Bush and Vice President Dick Cheney. He served 4 years and 9 months in prison before being deported to India upon release. Buddhi was born to Syamala Buddhi and Captain Buddhi K Subbarao, whose father was a senior defence scientist in the Indian navy and had been tried in 1988 for leaking naval secrets; he was acquitted in 1993 after it was revealed that the alleged leaked information was his own Ph.D. thesis, a publicly available document. In December 2005 and January 2006, Buddhi posted messages on a Yahoo business discussion forum urging people in Iraq to retaliate against the Iraq war by killing President George W. Bush, Vice President Dick Cheney, and their spouses. His lawyer, Somnath Bharti, claimed that the indictment did not include any of the alleged charges and that the prosecution failed to prove Buddhi authored the messages. Buddhi had hacked the Yahoo accounts of thousands of Purdue University students and used those stolen credentials, along with a bot, to disseminate anti-Bush and anti-war messages across Yahoo's Discussion Boards. Buddhi was sentenced in 2007 to 4 years and 9 months in prison. He received support from alumni and staff of several Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs), who joined his father in lobbying for his release, as well as from External Affairs Minister SM Krishna and former U.S. President Bill Clinton.
